Серия 2 «Ужин при всех»: промпты для картинок

Настройки везде: формат 9:16, качество 2K, модель Nano Banana Pro (кадры блюд B1–B6 можно на 2.1). К каждому промпту прикрепите референсы в указанном порядке: номер 1 под фото, номер 2 следующим и так далее. Файлы лежат в папке louis_ep2/refs/ под теми же названиями R1–R5.

Vertical 9:16 hand-held phone photo, ultra-wide front camera look, slightly underexposed, a real photograph with fine film grain, matte skin with pores, photorealistic, no retouching, no beauty filter. The first frame of a video: the phone is held FAR TOO CLOSE to his face by a clumsy hand, ultra-wide distortion, soft focus. Framing like the SECOND reference image (take only its framing: extreme close-up, the face tilted about 20 degrees and off-centre to the right, nose and lips filling the frame, one eye at the lower right edge, the top half of the picture covered by a dark out-of-focus mass; ignore its phone interface and icons). The king (the king from the FIRST reference image, exactly the same man: pale chalk-white matte court powder over the whole face, clearly paler than his neck, muted grey-green eyes with heavy symmetrical upper eyelids and a haughty downward gaze, one eyebrow slightly raised, long straight nose, thin upturned waxed moustache, a small dark beauty spot beside the mouth, a light pink flush only on the cheekbones; visible pores and fine lines, no skin smoothing; a tall grey-white powdered wavy wig with a high swept-up front, rolled curls above the ears and long curls falling over both shoulders to the chest; a scarlet velvet coat embroidered with gold suns, a white lace cravat with a white linen napkin tucked into it) with his mouth slightly open mid-word and the haughty heavy lids. The dark mass covering the upper half is HIS OWN scarlet velvet sleeve with gold embroidery and his fist, very close to the lens. A little grey wig curl at the left edge, a blurred candlelit table and crowd behind. No text, no captions, no logos, no interface, no modern objects, no extra fingers.
